criteria.evidence: B1 is really fixed. I built my own fixture outside the repo (/tmp/.../b1) and ran --fix. `a11.md:11` became `a11.md:20`, so the filename was left alone. In `target.md:3-5` and `a11.md:11` on the same line, both were fixed: the range became 20-22 and kept its width. `target.md:2,105-107` became `20,105-107`, so the extra segments survived. The anchors are byte-for-byte unchanged (diff shows only the number segments changed). On rerun all four are OK, and the `[after-fix]` line gives the post-fix counts (N5 fixed). B2 is only partly fixed. When I copy the real `scripts/ledger-external.txt` into a temp root, `profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml:3193`「allowedModels:」 now resolves to `~\.dsh\profiles\web\cordis.patch.yml` and is judged OK. A bare `cordis.patch.yml` gives UNRESOLVED, so it no longer guesses. That much works. But `scripts/cite-check.py:144`「if len(hits) > 1:」 means the path-suffix check only runs when there are 2 or more in-project candidates. With exactly 1 in-project candidate it is returned directly, the directory part is never checked, and the external roots are never consulted. That leading `/` can never satisfy the target_ok suffix match, so `~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml:3193` and `~/.dsh/cordis.patch.yml:1` both come out UNRESOLVED. The repo already has 6 citations written this way (AGENTS-PATCH-2026-11-06 is one of 3 files using it). nonblocking.what: `apply_fix` uses `Path.write_text(...)` without passing `newline=`. On Windows this converts an LF file to CRLF wholesale. My fixture went from 364 to 371 bytes and `file` reports 'with CRLF line terminators'. All the current target files in the repo are already CRLF, so there is no real impact yet, but this contradicts '一个字节都不动' (not one byte touched). Harness case 12 reads the file back in text mode, so it cannot see this. Fix: `open(..., 'w', newline='')`, and compare bytes in the assertion.

After --fix it became `22-26`, but it should be `20-24`. The contract does not tell writers that a range anchor must come from the first line.
